title: Influence bound from derivative thresholds
statement: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube and let $p$ be a real-valued function on that cube. Suppose $f(x)$ is the threshold sign of $p(x)$ at every input $x$, and $p(x)\ne 0$ for every $x$. Then the total influence of the real-valued sign representation of $f$ is at most the uniform average over inputs $x$ of $\displaystyle \left|\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\,g_i(x)\right|$, where $g_i(x)$ is the sign of the discrete derivative of $p$ in coordinate $i$ at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
At every input, $f$ is the threshold sign of $p$
